title: The Dashboard needs the Reports permission, also checked when loading
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in as an owner/admin (or any user who has the Reports permission) on the build under test; a single workplace is selected.
  2. You also have a second sign-in for a user who does NOT have the Reports permission (set under Settings > Staff / Roles), so you can check what that user sees.
custom_steps:
1. Signed in as a user who HAS the Reports permission, look at the top navigation and confirm a "Dashboard" entry appears. (The Reports permission is the only thing that controls this — there is no separate Dashboard setting or switch to turn on.)
  2. Sign in as the user who does NOT have the Reports permission and confirm there is no "Dashboard" entry, and that you land on Work Orders after logging in.
  3. Still as the user without the permission, type the dashboard address straight into the browser and confirm it takes you to Work Orders rather than showing an error page.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The "Dashboard" entry appears for any user who has the Reports permission — that permission is the only gate, with no organization-level Dashboard feature and no other switch.
  • A user without the Reports permission does not see the "Dashboard" entry, lands on Work Orders after logging in, and is sent to Work Orders (not an error page) when opening the dashboard address directly.
  • Blocking the dashboard behind the scenes — so a user without the permission gets no dashboard data even if the entry were shown — is confirmed by the automated check, not something the manual tester verifies by hand.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-490, story SV-9573 (S1 — Access & Entry Point); Dashboard v1 specification, Confluence page 788430850, section S1; read on 2 October 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S1-R6: “The "Dashboard" entry is shown to any user who has the reportsPageAccess permission, the same permission that shows the "Reports" entry. That permission is the only gate: there is no organization-level Dashboard feature and no other switch.”
  • S1-R7: “The gate in S1-R6 is enforced by the server, not only by hiding the navigation entry. A request to any of the dashboard’s own endpoints from a user who lacks reportsPageAccess is refused with an authorization failure and returns no dashboard data. Hiding the entry is a convenience for the user, never the control.”
  • S1-R8: “A user who lacks the permission in S1-R6 lands on Work Orders. This applies both to where they land after logging in and to entering the dashboard address directly, which redirects to Work Orders rather than showing an error page.”

Last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026.
